DWG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph JAN 31 2020 MS. LORELIE B. MENDOZA, REB, REA OPINION NO. Consultant on Compliance Maria Clara St. San Nicolas, San Fernando, Pampanga Dear Ms. Mendoza: S. 202 This has reference to your letter dated 10 October 2019, concerning the authority of Sangguniang Panlalawigan to either approve or disapprove an application for reclassification of agricultural lands into non-agricultural uses. After thorough perusal of your said letter and its attachments, it is our understanding that, ultimately, herein issue concerns the validity of the subject directive of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Nueva Ecijal, being imposed to all Sangguniang Bayan/Panglungsod therein. As can be gleaned from the said directive, the same was issued pursuant to Section 20 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) as further bolstered in Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 54 series of 19932. In essence, said directive provides that all ordinances reclassifying the use of land submitted by the Sangguniang Bayan/PanIungsod to herein concerned Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review of the latter must be accompanied by the documentary requirements specified thereunder. Hence, two questions have been culled out, to wit: 1. 2. Whether or not the directive of herein concerned Panla/awigan is valid; and Whether or not herein concerned Panlalawigan has the authority to either approve or disapprove the application for reclassification of agricultural lands in light of the subject directive. At the outset, attention is invited to the pertinent provision of MC No. 54, series of 1993, specifically Section 3 thereof, viz: "SEC. 3. Review of ordinances reclassifying agricultural lands. — All ordinances authorizing the reclassification of agricultural lands shall be subject to the review and approval by the province in the case of component city or municipality, or by HLRB in the case ofa highly urbanized or independent component city in accordance with EO 72 (1993). " 1 Dated 8 August 2019 2 Entitled: Prescribing the Guidelines Governing Section 20 of RA 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 Authorizing Cities and Municipalities to Reclassify Agricultural Lands into Non-Agricultural Uses

As can be gleaned from the aforequoted provision, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan is mandated to review all ordinances anent reclassifying agricultural lands into non- agricultural uses enacted by component cities/municipalities. While it is true that the same did not specifically mandate the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to require additional requirements from the Sangguniang Bayan/Panlungsod concerned in review of their ordinances relative to reclassification of agricultural lands, Section 7 of Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) Administrative Order No. 01, series of 20193 provides that LGUs must have the proper Certificate of Eligibility for Reclassification of agricultural lands issued by the Department of Agriculture (DA) in accordance with D.A. A.O. No. 1 series of 2017. The DA certificate must be attached to the HLURB Certificate or the LGU Resolution, as the case may be, to prove that there is a valid reclassification. A close scrutiny of the documentary requirements set forth in the subject directive, it can be gathered that such documentary requirements appears to be of paramount consideration in the approval of an ordinance anent reclassification of agricultural lands, to see to it that the parameters that need to be taken into account are complied with. More importantly, the said documentary requirements are in accordance with Item VII of DA A.O No. I, series of 2017. Accordingly, we see no legal infirmity thereto. Coming now on the issue on the authority of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to either approve or disapprove the application for reclassification of agricultural lands. Section 20 of the LGC is categorical when it provides, viz: "A city or municipality may, through an ordinance passed by the sanggunian after conducting public hearings for the purpose, authorize the reclassification of agricultural lands and provide for the manner of their utilization or disposition in the following cases: (I) when the land ceases to be economically feasible and sound for agricultural purposes as determined by the Department of Agriculture or (2) where the land shall have substantially greater economic value for residential, commercial, or industrial purposes, as determined by the sanggunian concerned: Provided, That such reclassification shall be limited to the following percentage of the total agricultural land area at the time of the passage of the ordinance xxx" From the foregoing, we can discern that it is the city or municipality who have the power to reclassify agricultural lands provided that the conditions specified therein are complied with. Let it be emphasized however that such power is not absolute. Mere reclassification of an agricultural land does not ipso facto allow the landowner thereof to change its use. Such reclassified agricultural lands must apply for conversion before the DAR in order to use the same for the said purpose. The Supreme Court, in the case of Chamber of Real Estate and Builders Associations, INC. (CREBA) vs. the Secretary of Agrarian Reform (G.R. No. 183409) had this to say: "xxx Reclassification alone will not suffice to use the agricultural lands for other purposes. Conversion is needed to change the current use of reclassified agricultural lands. Subject: Streamlining the Processing of Applications for Land Use conversion under DAR Administrative Order No. 1, series of 2002.

It is of no moment whether the reclassification of agricultural lands to residential, commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural uses was done by the LGUs or by way of Presidential Proclamations because either way they must still undergo conversion process. It bears stressing that the act of reclassifying agricultural lands to non- agricultural uses simply specifies how agricultural lands shall be utilized for non-agricultural uses and does not automatically convert agricultural lands to non-agricultural uses or for other purposes. As explained in DAR Memorandum Circular No. 7, Series of 1994, cited in the 2009 case of Roxas & Company, Inc. v. DAMBA-NFSW and the Department of Agrarian Reform, 47 reclassification of lands denotes their allocation into some specific use and providing for the manner of their utilization and disposition or the act of specifying how agricultural lands shall be utilized for non-agricultural uses such as residential, industrial, or commercial, as embodied in the land use plan. For reclassified agricultural lands, therefore, to be used for the purpose to which they are intended there is still a need to change the current use thereof through the process of conversion. The authority to do so is vested in the DAR, which is mandated to preserve and maintain agricultural lands with increased productivity. Thus, notwithstanding the reclassification of agricultural lands to non-agricultural uses, they must still undergo conversion before they can be used for other purposes " Further, Section 7 of DAR A.O No. I, series of 2019 provides that the Sangguniang Bayan/Panlungsod Zoning Ordinance and the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Resolution approving said Zoning Resolution shall be submitted in applications for conversion in case of landholdings situated in Component Cities and Municipalities and the conversion is from an agricultural use to a non-agricultural use. Hence, query no. 2 should be answered in the affirmative. We hope the foregoing be sufficient to enlighten you on the matters presented herein. Very ul urs, ED . ANO Cc: Secr t ry RD JULIE J.
